question.problem:
Which of the following sets are orthonormal?

I. $U=\{[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}]\}$

II. $V=\{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 9\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}28 \\ -21 \\ -7\end{aligned}]\}$

III. $W=\{[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{5} \\ \frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{5} \\ -\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]\}$
question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of the given sets as 
$\{{u}_{1},{u}_{2}\},$ 
$\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}\},$ and 
$\{{w}_{1},{w}_{2}\},$ respectively. 

The sets $U,V,$ and $W$ are orthonormal if the following conditions on each set hold:

- ${u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{2}=0\,\text{and}\,\{\begin{aligned}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}=1 \\ {u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}=1.\end{aligned}$

- $\{\begin{aligned}{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{2}=0 \\ {v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{3}=0 \\ {v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{3}=0\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,\{\begin{aligned}{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}=1 \\ {v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}=1 \\ {v}_{3}\cdot {v}_{3}=1.\end{aligned}$

- ${w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{2}=0\,\text{and}\,\{\begin{aligned}{w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{1}=1 \\ {w}_{2}\cdot {w}_{2}=1.\end{aligned}$

With that in mind, let's examine our sets in turn.

- For the set $U,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}]=-\frac{3}{10}+\frac{3}{10}=0 & ✓ \\ {u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}]=\frac{9}{10}+\frac{1}{10}=1 & ✓ \\ {u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}]=\frac{1}{10}+\frac{9}{10}=1 & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, the set $U$ is orthonormal.

- For the set $V,$ notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=4+9+1=14\ne 1 & \times \end{aligned}
$$

So, $V$ is not an orthonormal set.

- For the set $W,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{5} \\ \frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{5} \\ -\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]=\frac{12}{25}-\frac{12}{25}=0 & ✓ \\ {w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{5} \\ \frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{5} \\ \frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}]=\frac{9}{25}+\frac{16}{25}=1 & ✓ \\ {w}_{2}\cdot {w}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{5} \\ -\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{5} \\ -\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]=\frac{16}{25}+\frac{9}{25}=1 & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, $W$ is an orthonormal set.

Therefore, we conclude that the correct answer is "$U$ and $W$ only".
